greeting.text: Klaus Lunettes, Golden Dawn. I assume you know what that means. If you do not, you will learn.
State your purpose in the Sanctuary. ...The dungeon, of course. Then listen carefully, because I will say this only once.
A new delver. Tell me, {player}: do you have a plan, or only courage? Courage is not a plan.
Hm. A delver of record already. Then I will skip the lecture. Mostly.
{player}. What have you learned since last time?
Still alive? Good. Dead delvers make poor strategists.

hint.text: Every dangerous attack shows its warning first: a mark on the floor, a glow, a held breath. Learn the warnings and half the fight is won.
Steel is patient. A wall, a lance, an ally standing behind both. Build a position before you advance.
Do not fight in the open when a corridor will do. Narrow ground favours the prepared.
I was raised to believe nobility is a privilege. I have since learned it is a debt. I intend to repay mine.
Noble or commoner, I judge a mage by how long they stay on their feet. The dungeon keeps the same ledger.
Noise and light draw attention in the dark. Move quietly through halls you have not cleared, and scout before you commit.
No champion defeated, yet you are asking for advice. That alone puts you ahead of most. Study the first guardian's pattern before you commit.
The Eye of the Midnight Sun fights as a unit. When you meet one of them, assume a second plan is hidden behind the first.
You defeated Vetto. A beast with no obvious weakness. I would like your notes, if you kept any.
Gravity, blood, bone. Three siblings, three problems. Solve them one at a time, in the order the Chronicle gives.
Lucius reads a single attacker's rhythm. So break your rhythm, or strike in pairs, or strike so fast he has no time to read.
I cannot evaluate enemies from worlds I have never studied. I will study them anyway. A strategist is paid to be uncomfortable.

farewell.text: Do nothing unwise. Or, at the least, document it.
